newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwandan-Zaire troops trade fire over border.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan-Zaire troops trade fire over border.

text.p: Rwandan and Zairean forces traded mortar and machinegun fire across their border on Tuesday, aid officials and other witnesses said.
Aid workers at the Cyangugu office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), which is close to the border, had to briefly take refuge in their residence from the firing, aid officials said.
Reuters Television producer Tony Wende in Cyangugu said forces in Zaire opened fire at about 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) and Rwandan army troops responded in an exchange lasting about two hours.
"It was a fairly sustained bombardment," Wende said. "The Rwandans fired mortars, anti-aircraft guns and heavy machine- guns with tracers."
"There is sporadic firing still as evening falls," Wende said, adding that he had not seen any casualties on the Rwandan side of the border.
The exchange of fire appeared to be the most serious since one in late September, aid officials said.
The firing, just across the border from the beleaguered Zairean town of Bukavu, follows fighting between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels.
A British Broadcasting Corporation correspondent in Cyangugu reported seeing smoke coming from a Zairean army position and said Rwandan troops set up new mortar positions near Zairean territory.
